status.en: 215 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 15% fewer than the week before, most of them in Lagos, Abuja and Kaduna.
status.nb: 215 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 15 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Lagos, Abuja og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen killed seven civilians in a Plateau community and shot Islamic cleric Yahaya Masussuka dead in Katsina, while troops captured bandits' logistics suppliers in Benue and foiled attacks on villages in Plateau and Borno, killing dozens of terrorists. A gang attack in Binnari, Taraba left at least 62 dead, and troops rescued two herders and recovered livestock in Zamfara after a bandit attempt. Military operations also destroyed a bomb-making hideout and killed two ISWAP commanders in Borno. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn drepte syv sivile i et samfunn på Plateau og skjøt den islamske lærde Yahaya Masussuka død i Katsina, mens tropper fanget bandittenes logistikkleverandører i Benue og avverget angrep på landsbyer i Plateau og Borno, og drepte dusinvis av terrorister. Et gjengangrep i Binnari, Taraba etterlot minst 62 døde, og tropper reddet to hyrder og gjenvant husdyr i Zamfara etter et bandittforsøk. Militære operasjoner ødela også et bombefremstillingshule og drepte to ISWAP-kommandoer i Borno. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
